requirements.title: The set and detection timing of input/output error conditions are processor dependent
requirements.definition: The set of input/output error conditions is processor dependent, and except where otherwise specified the occurrence or detection point of an error condition is processor dependent.

pending.io-error-condition-set-processor-depende: No portable oracle may require a processor to classify an implementation-specific situation as an I/O error unless another registered rule specifies it.
pending.io-error-detection-timing-processor-depe: No portable oracle may require a specific detection point for an otherwise unspecified I/O error; future tests observe only specified status outcomes after statement completion.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, named intrinsic status values where the standard names them, branch-target execution, or unchanged sentinel values where the source requires no definition. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific nonzero IOSTAT numbers are not asserted.

requirements.title: Nonadvancing input beyond the current record produces end-of-record except at stream end-of-file
requirements.definition: An end-of-record condition occurs when nonadvancing input attempts to transfer from beyond the end of the current record, except that a stream file whose current record is at the end of file produces end-of-file instead.

pending.nonadvancing-beyond-record-eor: Create an external formatted file with a short current record, initialize IOSTAT to a nonzero sentinel distinct from named constants, perform nonadvancing input past that record, and assert IOSTAT_EOR using the named constant rather than its numeric value.
pending.stream-final-record-eof-precedence: Create a formatted stream file with the current record at end of file, attempt nonadvancing input beyond it, and assert IOSTAT_END rather than IOSTAT_EOR using ISO_FORTRAN_ENV names.

requirements.title: End-of-file conditions cover sequential endfile records, internal-file exhaustion, and stream exhaustion
requirements.definition: An end-of-file condition occurs when an endfile record is encountered during sequential input, when reading beyond the end of an internal file, or when reading beyond the end of a stream file.

pending.sequential-endfile-record-eof: Write a known sequential external record followed by ENDFILE, rewind, read the data, then read again with IOSTAT initialized away from IOSTAT_END and assert IOSTAT_END.
pending.internal-file-beyond-end-eof: Use a one-record internal file, read the only record into a nondefault variable, then read again with IOSTAT initialized away from IOSTAT_END and assert IOSTAT_END.
pending.stream-beyond-end-eof: Write a finite stream file, position after its written data, read with IOSTAT initialized away from IOSTAT_END, and assert IOSTAT_END without inspecting storage-unit encodings.

requirements.title: End-of-file may occur at input-statement start, during formatted input, or during stream input
requirements.definition: An end-of-file condition may occur at the beginning of an input statement, during formatted input when multiple records are required by the input-list/format interaction, or during stream input.

pending.eof-at-input-start-permitted: No portable oracle may require a processor to defer an otherwise valid EOF until after partial execution; future EOF tests accept IOSTAT_END at statement completion.
pending.eof-during-formatted-input-permitted: Use a format requiring another record after establishing the first record; assert only final IOSTAT_END and defined prior transfers, not an intermediate detection instant.
pending.eof-during-stream-input-permitted: Use stream input beyond written data and assert IOSTAT_END after the statement, without requiring a particular detection instant.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10.3-12.12: IOLENGTH, error, end-of-record and end-of-file conditions, IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and restrictions on I/O statements (batch166). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. IOLENGTH's exact count is latitude but its direct-access RECL= suitability is planned; END=/EOR= conditions, IOSTAT_END and IOSTAT_EOR distinctness, zero on success and positive errors are planned portably; IOMSG unchanged on success is planned with a sentinel while condition-message text is never compared. Source accounting only.
